text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were slightly lower in afternoon dealings on Thursday, hurt by profit-taking but underpinned by support from ongoing sluggish German economic conditions, traders said. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.10, down 0.05 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended modestly higher and outperformed Bunds on Thursday, buoyed by a CBI business survey showing growth in the retail sector in January was only sluggish. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-04/32, up 02/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures recovered from lows hit after German unemployment figures and a weak demand OAT auction. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.90 down 0.01 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italy bond futures continued their remarkable climb defying many brokers' views as the BTP market still put its trust in Italian denials of a plan to delay its EMU entry beyond 1999, dealers said. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.41 down 0.14 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were narrowly mixed in late morning, focusing on the monthly employment report due Friday. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-29/32, down 04/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.76 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower on Thursday due to the yen's weakness versus the dollar. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.34, up 0.04 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Euro Eurobonds and emerging sovereign provided the focus in the primary market on Thursday. L-Bank's finance arm issued seven-year deals in marks and French francs, raising a combined 690 million Ecu. Both the 750 million mark and 2.0 billion French franc legs will be redenominated in euros after EMU after which they will be merged to form a euro Eurobond.
Houses involved said early response was good, particularly in marks where there was a shortage of seven-year paper. The mark deal was reoffered at a yield spread of 10 basis points.
J.P. Morgan and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were joint leads.
